references.text: Esau became a skillful hunter, a man of the open country, while Jacob was a quiet man who stayed among the tents. Isaac loved Esau because he ate wild game, but Rebekah loved Jacob.
God was with the boy, and he grew up. He lived in the wilderness and became an archer.
He was a mighty hunter before the Lord. That is why it is said: 'Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the Lord.'
Rebekah heard what Isaac said to his son Esau. So Esau went out into the open country to hunt some wild game and bring it home.
See that no one is sexually immoral or godless like Esau, who sold his birthright for a single meal. You know that afterward, when he wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected.
Clear contrast: Weapons are necessary to carry out a mission in Genesis, while they are removed as a sign of God's judgment in Ezekiel.
Contrast in the use of weapon symbolism: Isaac asks for bow and arrows to act, while God removes them from the enemy at judgment.
Contrast in role distribution: In Genesis, humans hunt game in the open country; in Ezekiel, humans (symbolically) become food for animals in the open country.
